ko.L: 다리오 왕 제4년에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 스가랴에게 임했는데, 아홉째 달 사일, 곧 기슬르 월이었다.
ko.B: 다리오 왕이 다스린 지 4년째 되는 해에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀이 스가랴에게 임했다. 그날은 아홉째 달인 기슬르 월 사일이었다.

decisions.choice: the fourth day of the ninth month, Kislev, in Darius's fourth year: early December 518 BC
decisions.reason: This is nearly two years after the night visions (1:7) and about halfway through the rebuilding of the temple, which was finished in Darius's sixth year (Ezra 6:15). Kislev is the Babylonian name of the ninth month, used also in Nehemiah 1:1. The modern date is worked out from the Babylonian calendar.

decisions.choice: Zechariah is named in the third person
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 1:7, a heading speaks of the prophet by name. Chapters 7-8 hold the prophet's answer to a question about fasting, given in several messages (7:4, 8; 8:1, 18).

decisions.choice: in the fourth year of Darius the king (L); of King Darius's reign (B); in Darius's fourth year as king (R)
decisions.reason: The dated heading follows the wording of 1:1 at each level. Here the Hebrew calls Darius "the king". Readable puts the date first and says "of the year" for the month, without converting to the modern calendar.

decisions.choice: the dated heading as Haggai and Zechariah 1:1; "Quisleu" as Nehemiah 1:1
decisions.reason: The date keeps the settled wording at each level, with no modern calendar; the month name is the published form of Nehemiah 1:1.

decisions.choice: passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R) for the narrative frame of chapters 7-8
decisions.reason: The dated heading and the account of the delegation are narrative, so they take the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and the passé composé at Readable; the LORD's messages are speech.

decisions.choice: the dated heading; "Kislevu" as Nehemiah 1:1
decisions.reason: The settled dated heading at each level ("wa utawala wa" at B, "wa Dario kuwa mfalme" at R); the month name is the published form.

decisions.choice: L in the Hebrew order; B and R in the Vietnamese date order; "Kít-lêu" as Nehemiah 1:1
decisions.reason: Days 1-10 take "mồng". Readable puts the full date first, as the English Readable does; the month name follows the published Nehemiah 1:1.

decisions.choice: the Kings date formula ("다리오 왕 제4년", "다스린 지 4년째", "왕이 된 지 4년째"); "기슬르 월" as Nehemiah 1:1
decisions.reason: Years in figures, months and days in words at Literal and Balanced and the day in figures at Readable, as the settled formula; the month name is the published form.

ko.L: 벧엘이 사레셀과 레겜멜렉과 그의 사람들을 보내어 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 은혜를 구하게 하고,
ko.B: 벧엘 사람들은 사레셀과 레겜멜렉과 그들의 일행을 보내어 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 은혜를 구하게 하고,
ko.R: 벧엘 성읍 사람들이 사레셀과 레겜멜렉과 그들의 일행을 보내어, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 은혜를 베풀어 주시기를 빌게 했다.

decisions.choice: Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech: the town of Bethel sent two men with their companions
alternatives: Bethel-sharezer sent Regem-melech and his men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be divided in more than one way. Bethel may be the subject, the town standing for its people, as cities often do. Or "Bethel-sharezer" may be one man's name, a Babylonian-style name formed with the name of a god, and he sent Regem-melech. A few take Bethel as the place to which the men were sent, but the question is put to the priests of the temple in Jerusalem (verse 3). The translation takes the first reading.

decisions.choice: Bethel: a town north of Jerusalem, resettled after the exile; Sharezer: a Babylonian name
decisions.reason: Bethel lay about twelve miles north of Jerusalem, and people of Bethel were among those who returned (Ezra 2:28; Nehemiah 7:32). Sharezer is a name of Babylonian form (compare 2 Kings 19:37), and Regem-melech may mean "friend of the king"; such names suggest men born in the exile.

decisions.choice: to entreat the favor of the LORD: to pray to the LORD and seek his goodwill
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "to soften the face", means to seek someone's favor (Exodus 32:11; Malachi 1:9). The delegation comes to worship and to ask a question.

decisions.choice: The people of Bethel (B, R); their men (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people of" for the town, as m1 reads it, and "their men" for the companions of the two. Readable says what entreating the LORD's favor means. The sentence runs on into verse 3, so Literal ends with a comma.

decisions.choice: "Shareza" as 2 Kings 19:37; "Regem-meleki"
decisions.reason: Sharezer keeps the published form of the same name; Regem-melech is new, formed in the usual way.

decisions.choice: "Sa-rết-xe", "Rê-ghem-Mê-léc"
decisions.reason: The forms set for Zechariah; 2 Kings 19:37 spells a different man's name "Sa-rết-se".

es.R: Debían preguntar a los sacerdotes del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos y a los profetas: «¿Debemos seguir guardando luto y ayunando en el mes quinto, como lo hemos hecho durante tantos años?».

vi.R: Họ được sai đến hỏi các thầy tế lễ ở đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân và các nhà tiên tri: "Chúng tôi có nên tiếp tục để tang và kiêng ăn vào tháng năm như chúng tôi đã làm bao nhiêu năm nay không?"

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에 [속한] 제사장들과 예언자들에게 말하게 했다. "제가 이 여러 해 동안 해 온 것처럼, 다섯째 달에 몸을 구별하여 울어야 합니까?"
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집의 제사장들과 예언자들에게 묻게 했다. "제가 여러 해 동안 해 온 것처럼, 다섯째 달에 계속 울며 금식해야 합니까?"
ko.R: 그들은 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전 제사장들과 예언자들에게 이렇게 물어야 했다. "저희가 여러 해 동안 해 온 것처럼, 다섯째 달에 계속 슬퍼하며 금식해야 합니까?"

decisions.choice: the fifth month: the fast that mourned the burning of the temple
decisions.reason: In the fifth month of 586 BC, the Babylonian commander burned the temple, the king's palace and the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8-9; Jeremiah 52:12-13). The exiles mourned the day with a fast. Now that the temple was being rebuilt, the people of Bethel asked whether the fast should go on. The answer comes at the end of chapter 8 (8:19), after the LORD has spoken about the heart of the matter.

decisions.choice: keeping myself apart: abstaining, keeping a fast
decisions.reason: The verb means to set oneself apart, and is related to the word for a Nazirite, who abstained from wine (Numbers 6:2-3). Here it means holding back from food and pleasures in mourning.

decisions.choice: I: the town speaks as one person
decisions.reason: The delegation speaks for the people of Bethel, using "I" for the whole community, as Israel often does in the psalms.

decisions.choice: we (R); mourning and fasting (B, R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "we", since the whole community asks. Balanced and Readable give "keeping myself apart" as "fasting" (m2), and "weep" as "weeping" (B) or "mourning" (R). The priests "who belong to" the house are the priests "of" the house.

decisions.choice: the question to the priests in 합쇼체, with "제가" (L, B) and "저희가" (R)
decisions.reason: The delegation speaks respectfully to the priests and prophets; the town speaks as one person at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says "we", as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: the LORD's answer begins with a question of his own
decisions.reason: The LORD does not answer the question about the fast at once. He asks whether the fasting was ever for him (verses 5-7), and reminds the people of what the earlier prophets said (verses 8-14). The direct answer comes in 8:18-19.

source.text: אֱמֹר֙ אֶל־כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּֽי־צַמְתֶּ֨ם וְסָפ֜וֹד בַּחֲמִישִׁ֣י וּבַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וְזֶה֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה הֲצ֥וֹם צַמְתֻּ֖נִי אָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Say to all [the] people of the land and to the priests, saying, When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh, and this seventy years, did you really fast for me, me?

en.L: Say to all the people of the land and to the priests, "When you fasted and mourned in the fifth [month] and in the seventh, these seventy years, was it really for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that you fasted, for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.B: Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: "When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and the seventh months for these seventy years, did you truly fast for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: Tell all the people of the land and the priests, "For seventy years you have fasted and mourned in the fifth month and in the seventh month. But were you really fasting for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Di a todo el pueblo de la tierra y a los sacerdotes: «Cuando {{plural_you:ayunaron|ayunasteis}} e {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} duelo en el quinto [mes] y en el séptimo, estos setenta años, ¿de veras {{plural_you:ayunaron|ayunasteis}} para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?
es.B: Di a todo el pueblo de la tierra y a los sacerdotes: «Cuando {{plural_you:ayunaron|ayunasteis}} e {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} duelo en los meses quinto y séptimo durante estos setenta años, ¿de verdad {{plural_you:ayunaron|ayunasteis}} por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?
es.R: Diles a todo el pueblo de la tierra y a los sacerdotes: «Durante setenta años {{plural_you:han ayunado|habéis ayunado}} y {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} duelo en el quinto mes y en el séptimo mes. Pero ¿de verdad {{plural_you:ayunaban|ayunabais}} por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?

fr.L: Dis à tout le peuple du pays et aux prêtres : « Quand vous avez jeûné et pris le deuil au cinquième [mois] et au septième, ces soixante-dix ans, est-ce vraiment pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} que vous avez jeûné, pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ?
fr.B: Dis à tout le peuple du pays et aux prêtres : « Quand vous avez jeûné et pris le deuil au cinquième et au septième mois pendant ces soixante-dix ans, est-ce vraiment pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} que vous jeûniez ?
fr.R: Dis à tout le peuple du pays et aux prêtres : « Depuis soixante-dix ans, vous jeûnez et vous prenez le deuil au cinquième mois et au septième mois. Mais était-ce vraiment pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} que vous jeûniez ?

sw.L: Waambie watu wote wa nchi na makuhani, ukisema, "Mlipofunga na kuomboleza katika [mwezi wa] tano na wa saba, miaka hii sabini, je, kweli mlifunga kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}?
sw.B: Waambie watu wote wa nchi na makuhani: "Mlipofunga na kuomboleza katika mwezi wa tano na wa saba kwa miaka hii sabini, je, kweli mlifunga kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?
sw.R: Waambie watu wote wa nchi na makuhani, "Kwa miaka sabini mmefunga na kuomboleza katika mwezi wa tano na katika mwezi wa saba. Lakini je, kweli mlikuwa mkifunga kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?

vi.L: Hãy nói với toàn dân trong xứ và với các thầy tế lễ rằng: "Khi các ngươi kiêng ăn và than khóc vào [tháng] thứ năm và thứ bảy, suốt bảy mươi năm nay, có thật là các ngươi kiêng ăn vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không?
vi.B: Hãy nói với toàn dân trong xứ và các thầy tế lễ: "Khi các ngươi kiêng ăn và than khóc vào tháng thứ năm và tháng thứ bảy suốt bảy mươi năm nay, các ngươi có thật sự kiêng ăn vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không?
vi.R: Hãy nói với toàn dân trong xứ và các thầy tế lễ: "Suốt bảy mươi năm, các ngươi đã kiêng ăn và than khóc vào tháng năm và tháng bảy. Nhưng có thật là các ngươi kiêng ăn vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không?

ko.L: 이 땅의 모든 백성과 제사장들에게 말하여라. "너희가 이 70년 동안 다섯째 [달]과 일곱째 [달]에 금식하고 애곡할 때에, 참으로 나를 위하여, 나를 위하여 금식하였느냐?
ko.B: 이 땅의 모든 백성과 제사장들에게 말하여라. "너희가 70년 동안 다섯째 달과 일곱째 달에 금식하며 슬피 울 때에, 정말 나를 위하여 금식했느냐?
ko.R: 이 땅의 모든 백성과 제사장들에게 전하여라. "너희는 70년 동안 다섯째 달과 일곱째 달에 금식하며 슬퍼했다. 그러나 정말 나를 위해 금식했느냐?

decisions.choice: the seventh month: the fast that mourned the murder of Gedaliah
decisions.reason: Jewish tradition connects a fast in the seventh month with the murder of Gedaliah, the governor the Babylonians set over Judah after the fall of Jerusalem; his death drove the last of the people to Egypt (2 Kings 25:25-26; Jeremiah 41:1-3). The Day of Atonement also falls in the seventh month (Leviticus 16:29), but it was commanded in the law, and the fasts here are fasts of mourning added in the exile. The connection with Gedaliah is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: these seventy years: since the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: From 586 BC to this message in 518 BC was nearly seventy years, the time of judgment foretold by Jeremiah; see the note at 1:12.

decisions.choice: was it really for me: a question about motive, stressed by repeating "me"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the pronoun at the end, "for me, me?" The LORD asks whether their fasting was turned toward him, or was only grief for their own loss. Isaiah 58:3-7 asks the same of fasting without justice.

decisions.choice: for me ... for me (L); did you truly fast for me (B); were you really fasting for me (R); quotation marks
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated pronoun; Balanced and Readable show the stress with "truly" and "really". "Me" takes the setting for pronouns of God. The words Zechariah is to say are in double quotation marks, which close at the end of verse 7. Readable makes the long question a statement and a short question.

decisions.choice: "kwa ajili yangu, mimi"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated pronoun of the Hebrew; both free pronouns take the setting for God.

records.literal_gloss: And when you eat and when you drink, [are] not you the ones eating, and you the ones drinking?

en.L: And when you eat and when you drink, is it not you who eat and you who drink?
en.B: And when you eat and drink, are you not eating and drinking for yourselves?
en.R: And when you eat and drink, are you not doing it just for yourselves?

es.R: Y cuando {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}}, ¿no lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} solo para {{plural_you:ustedes mismos|vosotros mismos}}?

fr.L: Et quand vous mangez et quand vous buvez, n’est-ce pas vous qui mangez et vous qui buvez ?
fr.B: Et quand vous mangez et buvez, n’est-ce pas pour vous-mêmes que vous mangez et buvez ?
fr.R: Et quand vous mangez et buvez, n’est-ce pas seulement pour vous-mêmes ?

sw.L: Na mnapokula na mnapokunywa, je, si ninyi mnaokula, na ninyi mnaokunywa?
sw.B: Na mnapokula na kunywa, je, hamli na kunywa kwa ajili yenu wenyewe?
sw.R: Na mnapokula na kunywa, je, hamfanyi hivyo kwa ajili yenu wenyewe tu?

vi.L: Và khi các ngươi ăn và khi các ngươi uống, chẳng phải chính các ngươi ăn và chính các ngươi uống sao?
vi.B: Còn khi các ngươi ăn uống, chẳng phải các ngươi ăn uống cho chính mình sao?
vi.R: Còn khi các ngươi ăn uống, chẳng phải các ngươi chỉ làm cho chính mình sao?

ko.L: 또 너희가 먹을 때와 마실 때에, 먹는 것도 너희이고 마시는 것도 너희가 아니냐?
ko.B: 또 너희가 먹고 마실 때에, 너희 자신을 위해 먹고 마신 것이 아니냐?
ko.R: 또 너희가 먹고 마실 때에도, 그저 너희 자신을 위해 그렇게 한 것이 아니냐?

decisions.choice: is it not you who eat and you who drink: your feasting, like your fasting, is for yourselves
decisions.reason: The stress falls on "you". Whether they fast or feast, the people are thinking of themselves, not of the LORD. Religion that serves only the worshiper is empty.

decisions.choice: for yourselves (B); just for yourselves (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the stressed "you" means.

source.text: הֲל֣וֹא אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ בְּיַד֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֣ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֔ים בִּהְי֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יֹשֶׁ֣בֶת וּשְׁלֵוָ֔ה וְעָרֶ֖יהָ סְבִיבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְהַנֶּ֥גֶב וְהַשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה יֹשֵֽׁב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [Are] not the words which proclaimed Yahweh by [the] hand of the prophets the former, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, and its cities around it, and the Negev and the Shephelah inhabited?

en.L: Are not [these] the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} proclaimed by the hand of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, and its cities around it, and the Negev and the Shephelah were inhabited?"
en.B: Are these not the very words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, along with the towns around it, and when people lived in the Negev and the Shephelah?"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke these same words through the prophets of long ago. At that time people lived in Jerusalem, and it was doing well. People lived in the towns around it, in the Negev in the south and in the western foothills."

es.L: ¿No [son estas] las palabras que proclamó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} por mano de los profetas anteriores, cuando Jerusalén estaba habitada y tranquila, y sus ciudades a su alrededor, y el Néguev y la Sefela estaban habitados?».
es.B: ¿No son estas las mismas palabras que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} proclamó por medio de los profetas de antes, cuando Jerusalén estaba habitada y próspera, junto con las ciudades de su alrededor, y cuando había gente que vivía en el Néguev y en la Sefela?».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo estas mismas palabras por medio de los profetas de hace mucho tiempo. En aquel tiempo había gente viviendo en Jerusalén, y le iba bien. Había gente en los pueblos de su alrededor, en el Néguev, al sur, y en las colinas del oeste».

fr.L: N’[est-ce] pas là les paroles que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a proclamées par la main des prophètes d’autrefois, quand Jérusalem était habitée et tranquille, avec ses villes autour d’elle, et que le Néguev et la Shéfela étaient habités ? »
fr.B: N’est-ce pas là les paroles mêmes que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a proclamées par les prophètes d’autrefois, quand Jérusalem était habitée et prospère, ainsi que les villes d’alentour, et que des gens habitaient le Néguev et la Shéfela ? »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit ces mêmes paroles par les prophètes d’autrefois. À cette époque, des gens habitaient Jérusalem, et la ville était prospère. Des gens habitaient les villes autour d’elle, le Néguev au sud et les collines de l’ouest. »

sw.L: Je, [haya] si maneno ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyatangaza kwa mkono wa manabii wa kwanza, Yerusalemu ilipokuwa ikikaliwa na kuwa na raha, pamoja na miji yake iliyoizunguka, na Negebu na Shefela zilipokuwa zikikaliwa?"
sw.B: Je, haya si maneno yale yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyatangaza kupitia manabii wa zamani, wakati Yerusalemu ilipokuwa na watu na kufanikiwa, pamoja na miji iliyoizunguka, na watu walipoishi Negebu na Shefela?"
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema maneno hayo hayo kupitia manabii wa zamani. Wakati huo watu waliishi Yerusalemu, na mji ulifanikiwa. Watu waliishi katika miji iliyouzunguka, katika Negebu upande wa kusini na katika vilima vya magharibi."

vi.L: Chẳng phải [đây là] những lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền ra qua tay các nhà tiên tri thời trước, khi Giê-ru-sa-lem còn có dân cư và yên ổn, cùng các thành chung quanh nó, và miền Nê-ghép và vùng Sơ-phê-la còn có dân cư sao?"
vi.B: Chẳng phải đây chính là những lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền qua các nhà tiên tri thời trước, khi Giê-ru-sa-lem còn đông dân và thịnh vượng, cùng với các thành chung quanh, và khi miền Nê-ghép và vùng Sơ-phê-la còn có người ở sao?"
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán chính những lời ấy qua các nhà tiên tri ngày xưa. Thời đó có người sống ở Giê-ru-sa-lem, và thành rất thịnh vượng. Có người sống ở các thành chung quanh, ở miền Nê-ghép phía nam và vùng đồi thấp phía tây."

ko.L: 예루살렘과 그 주위의 성읍들에 사람이 살고 평안하였으며 네겝과 세펠라에도 사람이 살던 때에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 이전 예언자들의 손을 통하여 선포한 말씀들이 [이것이] 아니냐?"
ko.B: 예루살렘과 그 주변 성읍들에 사람이 많이 살고 번영하던 때에, 그리고 네겝과 세펠라에도 사람들이 살던 때에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 이전 예언자들을 통하여 선포한 말씀이 바로 이것이 아니냐?"
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 오래전 예언자들을 통해 바로 이 말을 했다. 그때에는 예루살렘에 사람들이 살았고, 그 성은 잘되고 있었다. 그 주변 성읍들과 남쪽의 네겝과 서쪽의 낮은 산지에도 사람들이 살았다."

decisions.choice: are not these the words: the former prophets said the same
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "are not the words", leaving "these" to be understood. The LORD points to what the earlier prophets said about fasting and worship without justice (Isaiah 58:3-7; Jeremiah 14:12), which verses 9-10 sum up.

decisions.choice: at ease: safe and prosperous
decisions.reason: The word describes a settled, peaceful life (Jeremiah 49:31; Psalm 122:6-7). The prophets spoke when the land was full and thriving, and it was lost because the people did not listen.

decisions.choice: the Negev and the Shephelah: the dry south and the low hills to the west
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry country south of Judah's hills; the Shephelah is the band of low hills between the hill country and the coastal plain. With Jerusalem and its towns, they make up the whole of Judah.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question (R); in the south; the western foothills (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question means, and says where the Negev and the Shephelah were. The closing mark ends the words begun in verse 5.

decisions.choice: "miền Nê-ghép", "vùng Sơ-phê-la" (L, B); "vùng đồi thấp phía tây" (R)
decisions.reason: The published forms of the place names (1 Samuel 27:10; 1 Kings 10:27); Readable says where the Shephelah was, as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 ... 선포한", without the honorific
decisions.reason: These are God's own words, given to Zechariah to say, so God names himself without -시-. Korean puts the "when" clause first, within the verse.

en.B: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Zechariah:
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Zechariah this message:

es.L: Y vino la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a Zacarías, diciendo:
es.B: Entonces la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a Zacarías:
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Zacarías este mensaje:

fr.L: Et la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie, disant :
fr.B: Puis la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut adressée à Zacharie :
fr.R: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné ce message à Zacharie :

vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho Xa-cha-ri sứ điệp này:

decisions.choice: a further word: what the former prophets said, and what came of it
decisions.reason: Verses 9-10 sum up the message of the earlier prophets, which still stands, and verses 11-14 tell how the ancestors refused it and were scattered.

decisions.choice: the formula with Zechariah's name
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording set for the prophets, with the prophet named in place of "me".

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱמֶת֙ שְׁפֹ֔טוּ וְחֶ֣סֶד וְרַֽחֲמִ֔ים עֲשׂ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, saying: Justice of truth judge, and loyal love and compassion do, each with his brother,

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Judge with true justice, and practice loyal love and compassion {{gender:toward one another|each man toward his brother}};
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Judge with true justice. Show loyal love and compassion to one another.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Judge fairly and honestly. Show faithful love and compassion to one another.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} con juicio verdadero, y {{plural_you:practiquen|practicad}} el amor leal y la compasión cada uno con su hermano;
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} con verdadera justicia. {{plural_you:Muestren|Mostrad}} amor fiel y compasión unos a otros.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} con justicia y honradez. {{plural_you:Muestren|Mostrad}} amor fiel y compasión unos a otros.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Rendez un jugement de vérité, et pratiquez l’amour loyal et la compassion {{gender:les uns envers les autres|chacun envers son frère}} ;
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : Rendez une justice vraie. Faites preuve d’amour fidèle et de compassion les uns envers les autres.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Jugez avec justice et honnêteté. Montrez de l’amour fidèle et de la compassion les uns envers les autres.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Hukumuni hukumu ya kweli, mkatendeane upendo usiokoma na huruma kila mtu na ndugu yake;
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Hukumuni kwa haki ya kweli. Onyesheni upendo usiokoma na huruma kila mmoja kwa mwenzake.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Hukumuni kwa haki na kwa uaminifu. Onyesheni upendo usiokoma na huruma kila mmoja kwa mwenzake.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Hãy xét xử theo công lý chân thật, và hãy thực hành tình yêu thương thành tín và lòng thương xót, mỗi người đối với {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} mình;
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Hãy xét xử theo công lý chân thật. Hãy đối xử với nhau bằng tình yêu thương thành tín và lòng thương xót.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Hãy xét xử công bằng và ngay thật. Hãy đối xử với nhau bằng tình thương không hề thay đổi và lòng thương xót.

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 진실한 정의로 재판하고, 각자 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}에게 한결같은 사랑과 긍휼을 베풀어라.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 진실하게 재판하여라. 서로 한결같은 사랑과 긍휼을 베풀어라.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 공정하고 정직하게 재판하여라. 서로 변함없는 사랑과 자비를 베풀어라.

decisions.choice: judge with true justice: give verdicts that are fair and can be trusted
decisions.reason: The words are addressed to all who settle disputes, from judges to elders at the town gate. "True" means faithful and reliable, a judgment that does not bend for a bribe or for the powerful (Ezekiel 18:8).

decisions.choice: loyal love and compassion: faithful kindness and tender mercy toward others
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is the loyal love that people bound together owe one another (see the note at Hosea 6:6). The second word is the compassion of a parent for a child (Psalm 103:13). The LORD asks his people to treat one another as he treats them.

decisions.choice: the message of the earlier prophets in a few words
decisions.reason: Justice, loyal love and care for the weak are the heart of the earlier prophets' call (Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:24; Micah 6:8; Jeremiah 7:5-6; 22:3). This, not fasting, is what the LORD asked.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R); toward one another / each man toward his brother (L)
decisions.reason: *Hesed* follows the settled wording for the prophets. "Each man toward his brother" means everyone toward everyone, men and women alike, so Literal gives it the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "one another". The sentence runs on into verse 10, so Literal ends with a semicolon.

decisions.choice: "cada uno con su hermano", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hermano" in this idiom already takes in men and women ("unos con otros"), so Literal keeps the Hebrew words without the gender setting the English has. Hesed is "amor leal" (L) and "amor fiel" (B, R).

decisions.choice: {{gender:les uns envers les autres|chacun envers son frère}}
decisions.reason: French has two wordings, as the English: the inclusive default and the traditional "each toward his brother".

decisions.choice: "kila mtu na ndugu yake", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "mtu" and "ndugu" already include women, so Swahili needs no gender setting here.

decisions.choice: {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "anh em" reads as men only, so Literal gives the inclusive "anh chị em" as the default, as the style guide does for brothers and sisters.

decisions.choice: {{gender:형제자매|형제}}
decisions.reason: Korean "형제" is men only, so Literal gives "형제자매" as the default, as the style guide does; Balanced and Readable say "서로".

source.text: וְאַלְמָנָ֧ה וְיָת֛וֹם גֵּ֥ר וְעָנִ֖י אַֽל־תַּעֲשֹׁ֑קוּ וְרָעַת֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אַֽל־תַּחְשְׁב֖וּ בִּלְבַבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and widow and fatherless, sojourner and poor, do not oppress, and evil of each [against] his brother do not plan in your heart.

en.L: and do not oppress the widow and the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor; and do not devise evil in your hearts {{gender:against one another|each man against his brother}}.
en.B: Do not oppress the widow or the orphan, the outsider or the poor. And do not plot evil against one another in your hearts.
en.R: Do not mistreat widows, orphans, foreigners or poor people. Do not even think about how to harm one another.

es.L: y no {{plural_you:opriman|oprimáis}} a la viuda ni al huérfano, al inmigrante ni al pobre; y no {{plural_you:tramen|traméis}} el mal en {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}} cada uno contra su hermano.
es.B: No {{plural_you:opriman|oprimáis}} a la viuda ni al huérfano, al extranjero ni al pobre. Y no {{plural_you:tramen|traméis}} en {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}} el mal unos contra otros.
es.R: No {{plural_you:maltraten|maltratéis}} a las viudas, a los huérfanos, a los extranjeros ni a los pobres. Ni siquiera {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} en cómo hacerse daño unos a otros.

fr.L: et n’opprimez pas la veuve et l’orphelin, l’immigré et le pauvre ; et ne méditez pas le mal dans vos cœurs {{gender:les uns contre les autres|chacun contre son frère}}.
fr.B: N’opprimez pas la veuve ni l’orphelin, l’étranger ni le pauvre. Et ne projetez pas dans vos cœurs de faire du mal les uns aux autres.
fr.R: Ne maltraitez pas les veuves, les orphelins, les étrangers ni les pauvres. Ne pensez même pas à vous faire du mal les uns aux autres.

sw.L: wala msimdhulumu mjane, wala yatima, mgeni wala maskini; wala msiwaziane mabaya mioyoni mwenu kila mtu juu ya ndugu yake.
sw.B: Msimdhulumu mjane wala yatima, mgeni wala maskini. Wala msipange mioyoni mwenu mabaya dhidi ya mwenzenu.
sw.R: Msiwatendee vibaya wajane, yatima, wageni wala maskini. Wala msifikiri hata jinsi ya kudhuriana.

vi.L: và đừng áp bức người góa bụa và trẻ mồ côi, ngoại kiều và người nghèo; và đừng mưu tính điều ác trong lòng các ngươi, mỗi người đối với {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} mình.
vi.B: Đừng áp bức người góa bụa hay trẻ mồ côi, ngoại kiều hay người nghèo. Đừng âm mưu điều ác trong lòng để hại nhau.
vi.R: Đừng ngược đãi người góa bụa, trẻ mồ côi, người nước ngoài hay người nghèo. Thậm chí đừng nghĩ cách làm hại nhau.

ko.L: 과부와 고아와 나그네와 가난한 자를 억압하지 말고, 너희 마음에 각자 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 해칠 악을 꾀하지 마라.
ko.B: 과부와 고아와 나그네와 가난한 사람을 억압하지 마라. 마음속으로 서로 해칠 일을 꾀하지 마라.
ko.R: 과부와 고아와 외국인과 가난한 사람을 괴롭히지 마라. 서로 해칠 생각조차 하지 마라.

decisions.choice: the widow, the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor: people with no one to protect them
decisions.reason: The law and the prophets name these four again and again (Exodus 22:20-23; Deuteronomy 24:17; Jeremiah 7:6; 22:3). A widow and a fatherless child had lost the man who stood up for them; a sojourner was a foreigner living in Israel without land or family; the poor had nothing to fall back on.

decisions.choice: devise evil in your hearts: plot harm in secret
decisions.reason: The "heart" is where plans are made. The command reaches behind deeds to intentions, which only God sees. 8:17 repeats it.

decisions.choice: the fatherless, the sojourner (L); the orphan, the outsider (B); orphans, foreigners (R)
decisions.reason: The words for the fatherless and the sojourner follow Jeremiah 22:3 at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "foreigners", the plainest word for someone living away from their own people. "Against one another" takes the gender setting at Literal, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "inmigrante" (L, as Deuteronomy 27:19); "extranjero" (B, R, as Jeremiah 22:3)
decisions.reason: The published words for the sojourner at each level.

source.text: וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לְהַקְשִׁ֔יב וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ כָתֵ֖ף סֹרָ֑רֶת וְאָזְנֵיהֶ֖ם הִכְבִּ֥ידוּ מִשְּׁמֽוֹעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they refused to pay attention, and they gave a shoulder stubborn, and their ears they made heavy from hearing.

en.L: But they refused to pay attention, and they turned a stubborn shoulder, and they made their ears heavy so as not to hear.
en.B: But they refused to pay attention. They turned their shoulders away stubbornly and stopped up their ears so that they would not hear.
en.R: But your ancestors refused to listen. They stubbornly turned away and covered their ears so they could not hear.

es.L: Pero ellos se negaron a prestar atención, y volvieron un hombro terco, e hicieron pesados sus oídos para no oír.
es.B: Pero se negaron a prestar atención. Con terquedad volvieron la espalda y se taparon los oídos para no oír.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} se negaron a escuchar. Con terquedad dieron la espalda y se taparon los oídos para no oír.

fr.L: Mais ils ont refusé d’être attentifs, ils ont présenté une épaule rebelle, et ils ont rendu leurs oreilles pesantes pour ne pas entendre.
fr.B: Mais ils ont refusé d’être attentifs. Ils ont obstinément tourné le dos et se sont bouché les oreilles pour ne pas entendre.
fr.R: Mais vos ancêtres ont refusé d’écouter. Ils se sont détournés avec obstination et se sont bouché les oreilles pour ne pas entendre.

sw.L: Lakini wakakataa kusikiliza, wakageuza bega la ukaidi, wakayafanya masikio yao mazito wasisikie.
sw.B: Lakini walikataa kusikiliza. Waligeuza mabega yao kwa ukaidi na kuziba masikio yao ili wasisikie.
sw.R: Lakini babu zenu walikataa kusikiliza. Waligeuka kwa ukaidi, wakaziba masikio yao ili wasisikie.

vi.L: Nhưng chúng đã từ chối lắng nghe, quay vai cứng cỏi, và làm cho tai mình nặng để khỏi nghe.
vi.B: Nhưng chúng không chịu lắng nghe. Chúng ương ngạnh quay lưng đi và bịt tai lại để khỏi nghe.
vi.R: Nhưng tổ tiên các ngươi không chịu nghe. Chúng ương ngạnh quay đi và bịt tai lại để không nghe thấy.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 귀를 기울이기를 거절하고, 고집스러운 어깨를 돌리고, 듣지 않으려고 자기 귀를 무겁게 했다.
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 귀 기울이기를 거절했다. 고집스럽게 등을 돌리고, 듣지 않으려고 귀를 막았다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희 조상들은 들으려 하지 않았다. 고집스럽게 돌아서서, 듣지 않으려고 귀를 막았다.

decisions.choice: a stubborn shoulder: like an ox that will not take the yoke
decisions.reason: The picture is of an animal pulling its shoulder away from the yoke (Nehemiah 9:29; Hosea 4:16). The ancestors would not submit to the LORD's word.

decisions.choice: they made their ears heavy: they made themselves deaf
decisions.reason: "Heavy" ears are ears that will not hear (Isaiah 6:10). The people chose not to listen.

decisions.choice: they: the ancestors, who heard the earlier prophets
decisions.reason: The verse continues the story of the generations before the exile, whose refusal led to their scattering (verse 14; compare 1:4).

decisions.choice: your ancestors (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, which the Hebrew leaves to the context.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}
decisions.reason: Readable names the ancestors as the hearers' own, so the possessive takes the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level in 7:11-14
decisions.reason: Verses 11-14 are the LORD's own words about the past ("says the LORD of hosts", verse 13), so they are speech and take the passé composé, not the passé simple of the narrative frame.

source.text: וְלִבָּ֞ם שָׂ֣מוּ שָׁמִ֗יר מִ֠שְּׁמוֹעַ אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֜ח יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בְּרוּח֔וֹ בְּיַ֖ד הַנְּבִיאִ֣ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי֙ קֶ֣צֶף גָּד֔וֹל מֵאֵ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And their heart they made diamond from hearing the instruction and the words which sent Yahweh of hosts by his Spirit by [the] hand of the prophets the former; and there was wrath great from Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And they made their hearts [like] diamond, so as not to hear the instruction and the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit by the hand of the former prophets; and great wrath came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: They made their hearts as hard as diamond so that they would not listen to the instruction and the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies had sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great wrath came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: They made their hearts as hard as rock so they would not listen to the teaching and the messages that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies had sent by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit through the prophets of long ago. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies became very angry.

es.L: E hicieron su corazón [como] diamante, para no oír la instrucción y las palabras que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos envió por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu por mano de los profetas anteriores; y vino gran ira de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Endurecieron su corazón como el diamante para no escuchar la instrucción y las palabras que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos había enviado por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu por medio de los profetas de antes. Por eso vino gran ira de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Endurecieron su corazón como una roca para no escuchar la enseñanza y los mensajes que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos había enviado por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu por medio de los profetas de hace mucho tiempo. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos se enojó mucho.

fr.L: Et ils ont rendu leur cœur [dur comme le] diamant, pour ne pas entendre la loi et les paroles que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées avait envoyées par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit par la main des prophètes d’autrefois ; et une grande colère est venue {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Ils ont rendu leur cœur dur comme le diamant pour ne pas écouter l’instruction et les paroles que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées avait envoyées par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit par les prophètes d’autrefois. Alors une grande colère est venue {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Ils ont rendu leur cœur dur comme la pierre pour ne pas écouter l’enseignement et les messages que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées avait envoyés par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit par les prophètes d’autrefois. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées s’est mis très en colère.

sw.L: Nao wakaifanya mioyo yao [kama] almasi, wasije wakaisikia sheria na maneno ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi aliyatuma kwa Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa mkono wa manabii wa kwanza; kwa hiyo ghadhabu kuu ikatoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Waliifanya mioyo yao kuwa migumu kama almasi ili wasisikilize mafundisho na maneno ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi alikuwa ameyatuma kwa Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kupitia manabii wa zamani. Kwa hiyo ghadhabu kuu ikaja kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Waliifanya mioyo yao kuwa migumu kama mwamba ili wasisikilize mafundisho na jumbe ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi alikuwa ametuma kwa Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kupitia manabii wa zamani. Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi akakasirika sana.

vi.L: Chúng làm cho lòng mình [cứng như] kim cương, để khỏi nghe luật pháp và những lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã gửi đến bởi Thần Linh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua tay các nhà tiên tri thời trước; vì vậy cơn thịnh nộ lớn đã đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.B: Chúng làm cho lòng mình cứng như kim cương để khỏi nghe lời dạy dỗ và những lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã gửi đến bởi Thần Linh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua các nhà tiên tri thời trước. Vì thế cơn thịnh nộ lớn đã đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.R: Chúng làm cho lòng mình cứng như đá để không nghe lời dạy dỗ và các sứ điệp {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã gửi đến bởi Thần Linh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} qua các nhà tiên tri ngày xưa. Vì thế {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã rất giận.

ko.L: 그들은 자기 마음을 금강석[처럼] 굳게 하여, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 자기 영으로 이전 예언자들의 손을 빌려 보낸 가르침과 말씀을 듣지 않았다. 그래서 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 큰 진노가 나왔다.
ko.B: 그들은 마음을 금강석처럼 굳게 하여, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 자기 영으로 이전 예언자들을 통하여 보낸 가르침과 말씀을 듣지 않았다. 그래서 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 큰 진노가 내렸다.
ko.R: 그들은 마음을 바위처럼 굳게 하여, 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 자기 영으로 오래전 예언자들을 통해 보낸 가르침과 말씀을 듣지 않았다. 그래서 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 크게 노했다.

decisions.choice: diamond: the hardest stone
decisions.reason: The word names a very hard stone, used as the point of an engraving tool (Jeremiah 17:1) and as a picture of a hard forehead (Ezekiel 3:9). Whether it was diamond, emery or flint, the point is the same: their hearts could not be marked.

decisions.choice: the instruction: God's law and teaching
decisions.reason: The word is *torah*, God's instruction, which the prophets called the people back to.

decisions.choice: by his Spirit through the former prophets: the prophets spoke by God's Spirit
decisions.reason: The words the prophets spoke were sent by the LORD through his Spirit. Nehemiah 9:30 says the same: "you warned them by your Spirit through your prophets."

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R); Spirit, capitalized; as hard as rock (R)
decisions.reason: *Torah* follows the wording set in Isaiah. The Spirit is God's Spirit, so it is capitalized, and "his" takes the setting for pronouns of God. Readable says "rock", a common picture of hardness.

decisions.choice: "luật pháp" (L); "lời dạy dỗ" (B, R) for torah
decisions.reason: Torah follows the English levels: the law at Literal, instruction and teaching at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: no honorific for the LORD here ("{{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 ... 보낸"; "거느린" at R)
decisions.reason: Verses 11-14 are the LORD's own words (verse 13), and God never takes -시- in his own mouth, even when he names himself in the third person. Torah is "가르침", the English "instruction" and "teaching".

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י כַאֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֖א וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ כֵּ֤ן יִקְרְאוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֔ע אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, just as he called and not they listened, so they will call and not I will listen, says Yahweh of hosts,

en.L: And just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: Just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called to them, but they would not listen. So when they called out, I would not listen, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Y así como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} llamó y ellos no escucharon, así ellos llamaron y yo no escuché, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Así como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} llamó y ellos no quisieron escuchar, así también ellos clamaron y yo no quise escuchar, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los llamó, pero ellos no quisieron escuchar. Por eso, cuando ellos clamaron, yo no quise escuchar, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a appelé et qu’ils n’ont pas écouté, ainsi ils ont appelé et je n’ai pas écouté, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait appelé sans qu’ils veuillent écouter, de même ils ont appelé et je n’ai pas voulu écouter, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a appelés, mais ils n’ont pas voulu écouter. Alors, quand ils ont appelé, je n’ai pas voulu écouter, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Ikawa, kama {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyoita nao hawakusikiliza, ndivyo wao walivyoita {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} sikusikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Kama vile {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyoita nao hawakutaka kusikiliza, vivyo hivyo wao waliita {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} sikutaka kusikiliza, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaita, lakini hawakutaka kusikiliza. Kwa hiyo walipoita, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sikutaka kusikiliza, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

vi.L: Và xảy ra rằng, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gọi mà chúng không nghe, thì chúng kêu và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng không nghe, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.B: Như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gọi mà chúng không chịu nghe, thì khi chúng kêu cầu, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng không nghe, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã gọi chúng, nhưng chúng không chịu nghe. Vì thế khi chúng kêu cầu, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng không nghe, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

ko.L: 그가 불렀으나 그들이 듣지 않았던 것과 같이, 그들이 불렀으나 나도 듣지 않았다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.B: 그가 불렀을 때 그들이 듣지 않았던 것처럼, 그들이 부르짖을 때 나도 듣지 않았다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 그들을 불렀지만, 그들은 들으려 하지 않았다. 그래서 그들이 부르짖을 때 나도 듣지 않았다. 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: he called ... I would not listen: the prophet's words become the LORD's own
decisions.reason: The verse begins by speaking of the LORD as "he" and ends with the LORD speaking as "I". Prophets often move from one to the other, because they speak for him.

decisions.choice: they would not listen, so I would not listen: the people received what they had given
decisions.reason: The same warning is in Proverbs 1:24-28, Jeremiah 11:11 and Micah 3:4: those who refuse to hear God's call will find that he does not answer their cry in the day of trouble.

decisions.choice: they called: in their distress, when disaster came
decisions.reason: The verb form often looks to the future, but here it tells what used to happen, as the story of the past goes on into verse 14.

decisions.choice: he, with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: "He" is the LORD, so it takes the setting for pronouns of God. Readable names the LORD at the start to make the change of speaker clear.

decisions.choice: spans on "yeye", "nami" and "mimi"
decisions.reason: The free pronouns for the LORD, "he" and "I", take the setting; the verb prefixes cannot.

decisions.choice: "그가" for the LORD, with no honorific; "…가 말한다" for 'amar YHWH
decisions.reason: The verse is the LORD's own speech, which moves from "he" to "I" (meaning decision m1); God takes no -시- in his own mouth.

records.literal_gloss: And I stormed them away among all the nations whom not they had known, and the land was desolate behind them, from passing through and from returning; and they made a land of delight into a desolation.

en.L: And I scattered them with a storm among all the nations whom they had not known; and the land behind them was left desolate, with no one coming or going; and they made the pleasant land a desolation.
en.B: I scattered them like a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known. The land they left behind was so desolate that no one came or went. They turned the pleasant land into a wasteland.
en.R: I scattered them like a storm scatters things, among nations they had never known. The land they left behind became so empty that no one came or went. They turned that beautiful land into a desert.

es.L: Y los dispersé con torbellino entre todas las naciones que no habían conocido; y la tierra quedó desolada tras ellos, sin nadie que fuera ni viniera; y convirtieron la tierra agradable en desolación.
es.B: Los dispersé como un torbellino entre todas las naciones que no conocían. La tierra que dejaron atrás quedó tan desolada que nadie iba ni venía. Convirtieron la tierra agradable en un lugar desolado.
es.R: Los dispersé como una tormenta dispersa las cosas, entre naciones que nunca habían conocido. La tierra que dejaron atrás quedó tan vacía que nadie iba ni venía. Convirtieron aquella hermosa tierra en un desierto.

fr.L: Et je les ai dispersés par la tempête parmi toutes les nations qu’ils ne connaissaient pas ; et le pays derrière eux a été dévasté, sans personne qui passe ni qui revienne ; et ils ont fait du pays de délices une désolation.
fr.B: Je les ai dispersés comme un tourbillon parmi toutes les nations qu’ils ne connaissaient pas. Le pays qu’ils ont laissé derrière eux est devenu si désolé que personne n’y allait ni n’en venait. Ils ont fait du pays de délices un désert.
fr.R: Je les ai dispersés comme une tempête emporte tout, parmi des nations qu’ils n’avaient jamais connues. Le pays qu’ils ont laissé derrière eux est devenu si vide que personne n’y passait plus. Ils ont fait de ce beau pays un désert.

sw.L: Nami nikawatawanya kwa tufani kati ya mataifa yote ambayo hawakuyajua; na nchi ikabaki ukiwa nyuma yao, hakuna aliyepita wala kurudi; nao wakaifanya nchi ya kupendeza kuwa ukiwa.
sw.B: Niliwatawanya kama kimbunga kati ya mataifa yote ambayo hawakuyajua. Nchi waliyoiacha nyuma ikawa ukiwa kiasi kwamba hakuna mtu aliyekwenda wala kurudi. Waliigeuza nchi ya kupendeza kuwa jangwa.
sw.R: Niliwatawanya kama dhoruba inavyotawanya vitu, kati ya mataifa ambayo hawakuwahi kuyajua. Nchi waliyoiacha nyuma ikawa tupu kiasi kwamba hakuna aliyekwenda wala kurudi. Waliigeuza nchi ile nzuri kuwa jangwa.

vi.L: Ta đã dùng bão tố phân tán chúng giữa mọi dân tộc mà chúng không hề biết; và đất bị bỏ hoang phía sau chúng, không ai qua lại; và chúng đã biến xứ tốt đẹp thành nơi hoang tàn.
vi.B: Ta đã phân tán chúng như cơn gió lốc giữa mọi dân tộc chúng không hề biết. Đất chúng bỏ lại trở nên hoang vắng đến nỗi không ai qua lại. Chúng đã biến xứ tốt đẹp thành nơi hoang tàn.
vi.R: Ta đã phân tán chúng như cơn bão thổi tung mọi vật, đến giữa những dân tộc chúng chưa từng biết. Đất chúng bỏ lại trở nên trống vắng đến nỗi không ai qua lại. Chúng đã biến xứ xinh đẹp ấy thành sa mạc.

ko.L: 내가 그들을 그들이 알지 못하던 모든 민족들 가운데로 폭풍으로 흩어 버렸다. 그들이 떠난 뒤에 그 땅은 황폐하여 오가는 사람이 없었다. 그들이 기쁨의 땅을 황폐한 곳으로 만들었다.
ko.B: 내가 그들을 회오리바람처럼 그들이 알지 못하던 모든 민족 가운데로 흩어 버렸다. 그들이 남기고 간 땅은 황폐해져서 오가는 사람이 없었다. 그들이 그 아름다운 땅을 황무지로 만들어 버린 것이다.
ko.R: 폭풍이 물건을 날려 버리듯, 내가 그들을 그들이 전혀 알지 못하던 민족들 가운데로 흩어 버렸다. 그들이 남기고 간 땅은 텅 비어서 오가는 사람이 없었다. 그들은 그 아름다운 땅을 사막으로 만들어 버렸다.

decisions.choice: I scattered them with a storm: drove them away as a whirlwind blows things away
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a storm or whirlwind (Habakkuk 3:14). The exile swept the people away suddenly and far.

decisions.choice: with no one coming or going: no traffic at all
decisions.reason: "Passing through and returning" means people traveling back and forth. The land was empty of all travelers (Ezekiel 35:7).

decisions.choice: the pleasant land: the land God gave as a treasure
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in Jeremiah 3:19 ("a pleasant land, the most beautiful heritage") and Psalm 106:24. The people's own sin turned the land of delight into a wasteland. Chapter 8 turns from this past to the promise of what the LORD will now do.

decisions.choice: like a whirlwind (B); like a storm scatters things (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the picture in the verb into a comparison. "Pleasant land" (L, B) becomes "beautiful land" (R).
